title: IntentGraph
description: The usage-ranking read model (ADR-0014): clusters of past queries, each carrying weighted edges to the capabilities invoked after them. Produced by two independent builders — the in-process local learner in ratel-ai-core and the hosted Ratel Cloud builder — and consumed as a scoring arm alongside BM25/dense retrieval. NOT a synced wire artifact in v1: it has no ETag semantics and is not served by GET /v1/catalog. It is specified here because it is the contract shared between those two producers, so neither can silently become the definition.

v.description: Graph schema version. A consumer MUST reject a version it does not know rather than degrade.

built_from_ts.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch of the newest event folded into this graph. Provenance only — it reports how current the graph is and is never read during ranking.

model.description: OPTIONAL fingerprint of the embedding model the centroids were built with. Present only for a graph that carries centroids; absent for a lexically-clustered graph. A consumer MUST NOT cosine a query against centroids built by a different model — it detects the swap (dimension or fingerprint) and pauses the usage arm until the graph is rebuilt. See ADR-0014.

cluster_policy.description: OPTIONAL policy the graph's existing cluster boundaries were drawn under: `similarity` is the minimum cosine a query must clear against a single member, and `coverage` the share of a cluster's members it must clear it against. Both are configurable per catalog, so a graph MUST record what it was clustered under — without it, two producers at different settings disagree about what a cluster means while both claiming v: 1. Absent means the built-in defaults (0.70 / 0.5), which is historically exact: before the policy was configurable those were the only values a producer could have used. PROVENANCE ONLY: it describes boundaries already drawn, not what a consumer should cluster at next, and changing the policy does NOT redraw them. See ADR-0014.

rev.description: OPTIONAL monotonic write counter, bumped once per mutation of the graph (a confirmed observation, a centroid rebuild). Never read during ranking — it is a primitive for the caller's storage layer, which owns persistence. Two uses: save-when-changed (persist only when `rev` differs from the last saved value) and stale-base detection (before overwriting a stored graph, compare its `rev` to the one you loaded; a higher value means another writer moved ahead — single-writer is the supported model, so this makes a clobber detectable, not merged). Absent means treat as 0; the counter continues up from there. See ADR-0014.

intents.description: The clusters. Order is not significant; consumers MUST NOT rely on it.

id.description: Cluster identifier, unique within the graph. Opaque: it names a row, nothing more.

label.description: Human-readable name for the cluster — the medoid member. Display only: retrieval results are identical whatever this string holds, so a producer MAY set it however it likes (the local builder counts it from the members; Ratel Cloud may use an extractor).

terms.description: Distinguishing keywords (c-TF-IDF over the members). Display only, like label.

members.description: THE MATCH KEY. The texts this cluster covers — raw user queries from the local learner, extractor-normalized goal strings from Ratel Cloud. Either works as a match corpus: a consumer with an embedder may derive a centroid from these, and one without may match lexically. This is why `centroid` is optional.

centroid.description: OPTIONAL precomputed mean of the members' embeddings, L2-normalized so cosine is a plain dot product. Absent when the producer clustered lexically rather than densely. A consumer MUST tolerate its absence and MUST NOT mix centroids across embedding models.

support.description: Count of distinct confirmed searches behind this cluster — searches that were followed by an invoke. One search that invokes several capabilities counts ONCE (it adds several edges but is one observation). Consumers scale the ranking arm by this (ADR-0014): one observation nudges, several carry full weight, so a single misclick cannot dictate ranking. Always >= 1.

seeded_support.description: OPTIONAL count of this cluster's `support` observations that came from a SEEDING pass — a baseline capture (queries recorded while Ratel observed but served no retrieval) or a replay of a trace log — rather than from live serving traffic. PROVENANCE ONLY: a consumer MUST NOT let it affect ranking, and a consumer that does not understand it MUST ignore it. Invariant: seeded_support <= support, since it counts a subset. Absent means 0.

cohesion.description: OPTIONAL tightness of this cluster's members: the norm of the UNNORMALIZED mean of their embeddings, before the `centroid` was scaled to unit length. 1.0 when every member points the same way, sqrt(n)/n for n mutually orthogonal ones. Normalizing divides this out, so it is the one thing `centroid` cannot tell a consumer, and a consumer with no per-member vectors needs it to know whether a match against `centroid` means anything: a diffuse cluster's centroid sits near the generic direction of its domain and is close to everything in it. Consumers SHOULD raise the similarity a query must clear in proportion (ADR-0014). Requires `centroid`; absent means 1.0, i.e. treat the cluster as tight.

vector_n.description: OPTIONAL count of embeddings folded into `centroid`. Distinct from members.len(), because a cluster can gain members lexically with no embedding. A producer that keeps learning needs it to weight the next fold correctly; without it a reloaded centroid counts as a single sample and one further observation can drag the whole cluster. PROVENANCE FOR LEARNING ONLY: a consumer MUST NOT let it affect ranking. Absent means 1.
vector_n.$comment: Absent means 1, not 0 — a stored centroid always had at least one vector folded into it.

last_ts.description: OPTIONAL epoch-millis of this cluster's most recent observation. Drives recency weighting and eviction (ADR-0014): a cluster keeps full weight for a grace period after its last use, then its arm weight decays and it is eventually evicted. Absent (or 0) means 'as current as the graph' — a loaded graph is not treated as instantly stale.

surfaced_tools.description: OPTIONAL map of tool id -> how many of this cluster's searches put that tool in front of the caller, counting only searches the caller then acted on. It is the denominator `tools` has never had: a tool shown twelve times and invoked once is indistinguishable from one shown once and invoked once when only invocations are counted. TOOLS ONLY — skill ids live in a different id space and are never recorded here. PROVENANCE ONLY: a consumer MUST NOT let it affect ranking, and a consumer that does not understand it MUST ignore it. An id present here but absent from `tools` has NO edge and MUST NOT be promoted — recording what a search returned is not the same as making it evidence. Absent means none were recorded.
surfaced_tools.$comment: Counts are >= 1: absence already means "surfaced no times", so a stored zero is a second spelling of the same state.

surfaced_skills.description: OPTIONAL map of skill id -> how many of this cluster's searches put that skill in front of the caller, counting only searches the caller then acted on. It is the denominator `skills` has never had: a skill shown twelve times and invoked once is indistinguishable from one shown once and invoked once when only invocations are counted. The skill-side twin of `surfaced_tools`; the two id spaces are why there are two maps. PROVENANCE ONLY: a consumer MUST NOT let it affect ranking, and a consumer that does not understand it MUST ignore it. An id present here but absent from `skills` has NO edge and MUST NOT be promoted — recording what a search returned is not the same as making it evidence. Absent means none were recorded.
surfaced_skills.$comment: Counts are >= 1: absence already means "surfaced no times", so a stored zero is a second spelling of the same state.

edges.description: Capability id -> count of confirmed invocations. Weights come from INVOCATIONS, never from what retrieval returned — recording the ranker's own output would reinforce its errors (ADR-0014). Only relative order within a cluster is load-bearing: the consumer ranks by weight and fuses on rank position, so absolute magnitudes never need reconciling with BM25 or cosine scores. MAY be empty. An id with no definition in the consumer's registry MUST be dropped, not ranked.
